subject: Caching assumptions & pricing sensitivity — Aeon Health discovery
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Dana Li <dana.li@aeon.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + hit-rate assumptions and next steps (Aeon discovery)

Thanks again for the time this morning — great conversation. Quick recap of the technical/pricing items we agreed to validate and next steps so we all have a single source of truth.

Call highlights (short):
- Aeon expects to run patient triage + summary flows and some document Q&A; many prompts are highly templated.
- Customer-reported nominal volume: ~40M tokens/month (combined input+output) with peak windows during mornings.
- Target effective price: Aeon said they want to be around $300 / 1M tokens (that was their internal goal).

Initial Redwood assumptions we discussed (to confirm):
- Prefix caching (100-token anchored prefixes) is applicable to ~55% of requests (templated prompts).
- Of that 55%, an initial on-prem/hosted prefix hit-rate estimate is 35% for steady-state traffic (so overall cache hit ~0.55 * 0.35 = ~19% of tokens).
- We modeled batch behavior separately; these hit-rate figures are for prefix-level reuse only.

Quick sensitivity we ran live: effective $/1M tokens (baseline list price $900 / 1M tokens for this model family) given prefix hits only:
- 0% hit: $900
- 20% effective hit: ~$720
- 40% effective hit: ~$540
(These are rule-of-thumb — full calc attached in redwood_hitrate_model_v1.xlsx)

Action items agreed:
1) Dana: share a 3-day sample of prompt logs (anonymized) so we can compute true prefix coverage and length distribution (help us confirm 55% estimate).
2) Aeon procurement: confirm budget range and month-to-month cadence (you mentioned an initial POC budget range earlier).
3) Monica: prepare a short sensitivity note showing effective $/1M across hit-rate bands (0/10/20/30/50%) and include a 12-month spend projection for FY28 ops.
4) Redwood: we will produce a draft quote that separates list model price from expected hit-driven effective price.

Attachments: redwood_hitrate_model_v1.xlsx (simple sensitivity workbook we used briefly on the call).

If any of the bullet points above need correction, please flag. Otherwise we can start with the prompt logs + procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior AE | Redwood Inference
From: Dana Li <dana.li@aeon.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + hit-rate assumptions and next steps (Aeon discovery)

Rishi — thanks for the summary and for the model. Correct on most points; a few clarifications from our side:

1) Volume: our estimate of ~40M tokens/month is based on expected POC traffic (3 clinics). If the POC goes well, we would scale to 120M tokens/month across 10 clinics in Q4.
2) Budget: the POC budget is tight — expected committed spend for the POC is in the $3k–$7k / month range. For enterprise rollout we can increase to mid/high tens of thousands, but that requires a pricing band that achieves sub-$400 effective $/1M tokens.
3) Cacheability: our engineering lead believes ~60% of prompts are templated (similar to your 55%) and many have short common prefixes (first ~80–120 tokens). We will extract sample logs and scrub PHI before sending.

I attached our procurement window and expected PO timeline (procurement-timeline.pdf). For next steps we can:
- Send the prompt samples by EOD Tuesday 6/1.
- Request a firm quote that shows both: (a) list price and (b) expected effective price given the 3 hit-rate scenarios you provide.

Thanks — we want to be pragmatic about the POC spend, so concrete numbers matter here.

—Dana Li
Director, Product Operations | Aeon Health
procurement@aeon.com
Attachment: procurement-timeline.pdf
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Dana Li <dana.li@aeon.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + hit-rate assumptions and next steps (Aeon discovery)

Thanks Dana — I pulled the quick sensitivity sheet into a short note and added the table below so everyone can align before we dig into raw logs. This is intentionally conservative and focuses on token-unit economics (does not include infra or SLA add-ons).

Assumptions: list model price = $900 / 1M tokens (single-region hosted); billing is per-token (in+out). Prefix cache policy: 100-token anchor (cache keyed on first 100 tokens).

Sensitivity table (effective $ / 1M tokens after prefix hits):
- 0% prefix hit: $900
- 10% prefix hit: $810
- 20% prefix hit: $720
- 30% prefix hit: $630
- 40% prefix hit: $540
- 50% prefix hit: $450

Notes on mechanics:
- The simplified math below assumes cached tokens are counted at a 0.1x token cost equivalent (i.e., when prefix is served from the cache the marginal per-token bill is 10% of a normal inference token due to KV reuse and local cache amortization). The workbook shows sensitivity if cache marginal fraction is 0.05x to 0.2x.
- If Aeon provides prompt logs that show higher than 60% templated prompts, the effective price moves favorably — but we should verify distribution of prefix lengths (shorter prefixes raise hit density but may reduce utility).

Quick ask: Dana, please confirm whether the ~40M tokens/month is expected to be evenly distributed month-to-month for the POC or whether you expect a ramp across the 3 clinics. That affects the recommended billing cadence and whether we propose a small reserved commit vs purely pay-as-you-go.

I'll take Rishi's action to prepare the sensitivity PDF and an example two-tier quote (POC and enterprise) once we have the logs.

—Monica
Pricing | Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Dana Li <dana.li@aeon.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + hit-rate assumptions and next steps (Aeon discovery)

Appreciate the succinct recaps. A few quick directions from my side so we don't lose momentum: 

1) Rishi — go ahead and prepare a two-sheet quote: (A) POC quote (month-to-month, shows list price and effective price bands for 10/20/30/40/50% prefix hits) priced to hit the low end of Dana's POC budget if possible, and (B) enterprise roll-out pricing that focuses on achieving <= $350 / 1M tokens at 40%+ effective hit. Include optional reserved-commit tiers.
2) Monica — include the alternative cache marginal assumptions (0.05x and 0.2x) in the quote appendix; that will make our sensitivity defensible to procurement.
3) Dana — thanks for the timeline. We'll accept the prompt logs next Tuesday; we'll scrub them on our end immediately and return a cleaned hit-rate diagnostic plus the quote within 48 business hours after receipt. If you prefer, we can run an initial sample analysis as soon as you drop 1 day of logs.

Rishi — once you have the draft quote, loop me in for a quick sign-off before sending to Aeon. I'd like to ensure the POC price doesn't bake in unrealistic hit assumptions.

Olga
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai
------
